Responsible for establishing and maintaining a comprehensive tracking system for all compliance-related projects. This includes documenting project progress, milestones, and any necessary updates or changes. Ensure that all project documentation is easily accessible to the relevant stakeholders.
Engage directly with project stakeholders to address any requirements, processes, or compliance-related inquiries. able to effectively communicate complex information in a clear and concise manner will be crucial to ensuring a smooth compliance process.
Support biosafety plans, coordinate chemical characterization and biocompatibility testing activities at CRO laboratories; understand testing needs; request quotes; coordinate test articles; and track schedules.
Support the creation and archiving of documentation that supports the biological safety of intuitive products; write reports and release them in the document management system (Agile)

Assist engineering teams in choosing patient-contact materials based on prior usage, and assist in describing design, material, process, and supplier modifications for biosafety evaluation.
The role involves supporting regulatory filing activities, including FDA 510(k) submissions (and other filing strategies), OUS country registration activities, MDR compliance certification, and other regulatory support needs.
Develop a working understanding of medical device biocompatibility, including relevant national and international standards, methods for biosafety end-point testing, and other regulatory requirements.

A minimum bachelor's degree in medical life science or engineering, or a master's degree, is preferred.
8+ years of experience in medical device product safety, product development, or related areas

Training in medical device biocompatibility testing and management, or an equivalent program, is preferred.
Proven project management skills: PMP certification is a plus.
Strong organizational and interpersonal skills are essential for working effectively in a team environment.
In vitro and in vivo laboratory testing experience is preferred but can be acquired through training.
Knowledge of MS Office applications

Primary Function of the Position
This position requires a candidate with extensive experience helping evidence generation strategy and execution of clinical studies. The Clinical Study Manager-4 (CSM IV) role will develop and execute strategies for clinical and outcomes research studies to help regulatory approvals and key strategic evidence initiatives. As a member of the Clinical Affairs team, this role will be accountable for working with key stakeholders to design and develop clinical protocols and execute clinical studies (pre-market or post-market studies), with minimal supervision. The candidate will be required to work closely with clinical research associates (CRAs), clinical trial assistants (CTAs) and data management for the conduct and execution of the study, as well as with biostatisticians to review and interpret results of clinical studies, develop clinical study reports, or help the development of clinical publications. During trial execution, the CSM will drive the progress of the trial during site selection, site start-up and through enrollment and follow-up. The CSM will clearly provide guidance to the monitors about monitoring needs, and oversee compliance work on the study. The CSM will also take a leadership role in external communication with investigators and study teams. The ideal candidate will have experience previously managing premarket studies in the United States and utilizing resources to research and scope research topics and to provide recommendations on clinical trial strategy. The candidate is also expected to have experience reviewing, interpreting and summarizing clinical literature.
Essential Job Duties
Accountable for leading assigned clinical research activities
Partner with internal stakeholders, investigators and KOLs to develop and review study design and concepts, prepare protocol and study outlines and subsequently driving identified initiatives
Accountable for the planning and execution of the clinical studies including site selection, review of potential patient recruitment and projections, creation of study related documents (protocols, case report forms, Informed consents, Clinical trial agreements, study reports), organizing IRB/EC submissions with follow-thorough to ensure successful progress
Accountable for autonomously conducting clinical studies on schedule and within budget while ensuring high quality and compliance
Perform on-site and remote site qualification visits, site initiation visits, interim monitoring visits and site close out visits.
Conduct clinical study monitoring to ensure regulatory and protocol compliance as well as overall data accuracy in accordance with the study clinical monitoring plan

Track study progress and provide regular status reports
Work closely with Biostatisticians on data analysis, interpretation and synthesis, in order to develop clinical study reports and /or help development of scientific publications
Track, process and manage site payments and help in study financial tracking by developing tracking tools as necessary
Organize and drive study meetings and other study activities as assigned
Mentor junior clinical study manager(s); provide guidance to CRAs and CTAs on monitoring and other study needs
Follow corporate (e.g., SOP’s) and regulatory requirements (e.g., GCP and US and OUS guidelines) and proactively manage studies, following such guidelines and requirements
Conduct literature searches and familiarize with literature to stay informed and abreast of relevant scientific/clinical knowledge and/or to establish evidence gaps
Critically appraise scientific literature and write clinical summaries to assist research and the development of clinical strategies and clinical investigational protocols
Review and revise Clinical Operations Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) to assist Clinical Affairs leadership with continuous process improvement initiatives
For post-market research, partner with commercial groups (i.e., marketing) to know about market trends and utilize information to help of business goals through Clinical Affairs activities
For post-market research, provide scientific expertise to the Health Economics and Outcomes Research department for development of outcomes research review (including identification of appropriate diagnosis or reimbursement codes, selection of clinical outcomes for procedures of interest)
Work with clinical investigators to prepare manuscripts, abstracts, slide presentations, and poster presentations for scientific meetings and publications in partnership with management
Help regulatory submission and approval of pre-market clinical studies and 510k(s), accountable for addressing regulatory body questions on clinical study design and results (e.g., protocol, ICF, eCRF, clinical study reports).
Required Skills and Experience
Previous experience implementing, helping and managing medical device trials Significant knowledge of clinical and/or outcomes research study design
Proven experience in protocol and ICF development, writing clinical section(s) for regulatory submission
Proven experience in conducting literature searches, reviews and appraisal of the scientific data
Excellent ability to interact with physicians and other professionals inside and outside the company
Knowledge of Good Clinical Practice ICH/GCP and other applicable regulations, fundamental knowledge of clinical research and monitoring requirements
Experience negotiating clinical research contracts and budgets
Must be able to work effectively on cross-functional teams
Must be able to travel 25-40% or based on business requirements
Must be able to manage multiple projects and/or manage different priorities
Proven communication, presentation and relational skills with high attention to detail and organization
Ability to learn quickly, tailor to shifting requirements, and self-educate on different surgical specialties as applicable to clinical projects (“Self-starter attitude”)
Ability to drive project team consisting of CRAs and CTAs and support management with relevant study updates
Exhibits solid work ethic to help meet tight timelines or multiple projects when necessary with a problem-solving mindset

Minimum advanced degree in a scientific/bioengineering field (M.S., Ph.D. or M.D.) with a minimum of 5 years of experience in clinical research, or Bachelor’s degree in a scientific/bioengineering field with a minimum of 8 years of experience in clinical research is preferred, or a minimum of 10 years of experience in clinical research with relevant training.
Preferred Skills and Experience
Accustomed to working in a hospital environment, experience working with nurses and surgeons preferred
Knowledge of statistics, statistical methods, and design of experiment is highly preferred

description:

The Sr. Manager, Financial Risk & Compliance will play a critical role in managing organizational risk, establishing policies and executing monitoring procedures, advising on the design of effective controls, collaborating with business teams to mitigate risks and promote best practices, and contributing to the overall success of the Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX) program to maintain the organization’s financial integrity.

Financial Reporting Risk Management
Develop, implement, and oversee risk management strategies, policies, and procedures related to financial reporting and operational processes.

SOX Program and Internal Controls
Oversee the design and enhancement of internal controls by partnering with process owners to ensure controls are effective, efficient, scalable, and aligned with financial reporting objectives.
Identify opportunities to simplify, standardize, and automate controls and compliance activities while maintaining an effective control environment.
Develop and monitor SOX and financial reporting control program metrics, providing insights and recommendations to improve program effectiveness, efficiency, and quality.
Drive continuous improvement initiatives that enhance the quality, consistency, and scalability of the Company's control environment and compliance programs.
Audit Coordination and Remediation
Coordinate directly with Internal Audit and external auditors to support walkthroughs, testing, deficiency evaluations, and remediation activities.
Lead the tracking and coordination of control enhancements and remediation efforts across process owners, ensuring timely implementation and sustainable outcomes.
Ensure the completeness, accuracy, and quality of audit and control documentation, including support for remediation efforts and management responses.
Governance, Training, and Program Enablement
Support governance activities related to the SOX program, including preparation of committee materials, executive reporting, action item tracking, and monitoring of key program initiatives.
Develop and deliver training, workshops, and educational programs to strengthen awareness of financial reporting risks, controls, and compliance responsibilities across the organization.

Exceptional root cause analysis skills to identify underlying factors contributing to risk and compliance issues, investigate complex issues, and propose effective solutions.
Excellent leadership skills with proven ability to influence and motivate others to drive results.
Effective verbal and written communication skills and ability to present complex topics in a clear and concise manner to audiences at various levels of the business.
Strong project management skills to ensure effective prioritization and timely execution to deliver the results.
Experience operating in SAP or similar ERP system, as well as the business and operational processes affecting financial reporting.
Strategic mindset to navigate organizational change to assess risks and make sound decisions with the growth and complexity of the organization.

Bachelor’s degree in accounting, finance or equivalent field required.
CPA or equivalent certification.

Big 4 or public accounting experience strongly preferred.

procedures.

description:
Job Description:
Job Description
Changing the World, One Kibble at a Time
Champion Petfoods is expanding! We are excited to announce we are looking for a Demand Finance Business Partner, North America to join our rapidly growing company.
Champion Petfoods is an award-winning pet food crafter with a reputation of trust spanning 35+ years. From our humble beginnings, founded in a small town in Alberta, Canada, Champion – with its ORIJEN® and ACANA® brands – is a key player in the global premium pet food industry.
Our purpose,  To Earn Pet Lover Trust Every Day so Pets Thrive for a Lifetime ,  provides the foundation for our highest aspirations as a company. Being a partner to the communities that surround us – and the environment that sustains us – are top priorities.
We would love to hear from you if you are passionate about personal and professional growth and see yourself as a key player contributing to our continued success as an award-winning company.
Here’s the scoop - Summary
The Demand Finance Business Partner, North America is a key strategic and commercial partner responsible for supporting the sales and demand functions in delivering their business and financial objectives. This role bridges commercial ambition with financial execution, serving as a trusted partner to the North American sales. marketing and leadership teams.
Balancing customer/channel dynamics, portfolio mix, pricing strategy, and trade promotions to drive sustainable growth is a central expectation of this role. Operating at the intersection of finance and commercial strategy, this position requires an analytically rigorous and commercially sharp professional who can turn complex datasets into actionable recommendations.
The role is both strategic and tactical, requiring the ability to identify high-level trends and risks while maintaining a hands-on approach to uncover root-cause insights and manage trade budget stewardship.
The Senior Manager, FP&A works out of our Corporate office in or Nashville (TN), Louisville (CO) or New York City (NY) and works a hybrid schedule with 3 days in-person and reports to the Finance Director, NORAM.
Key Responsibilities:
​ Commercial Performance & Revenue Optimization
Channel & Customer Profitability: Lead the review, analysis, and optimization of channel-specific and customer-specific profitability. Develop and maintain transparent performance views to highlight risk areas and unlock growth opportunities.
Route to Market & Portfolio Analysis: Analyze and optimize Route to Market (RTM) structures and portfolio margin profiles in close collaboration with Category Management and sales leadership.
Pricing & Revenue Management: Partner with the Strategic Revenue Management (SRM) team to execute pricing strategies, evaluate promotional elasticity, and ensure commercial alignment with overall financial targets.
Channel Specific Financial Support: Partner with the specific sales channels to model performance, evaluate go-to-market strategies, and drive Net Sales Value (NSV) and Gross Sales Value (GSV) optimization.
Trade Investment & Budget Stewardship
Trade Expenditure Management: Oversee the planning, forecasting, tracking, and controlling of the Trade Expenditure budget to ensure optimal financial discipline.
Promotion Effectiveness & ROI: Establish robust analysis frameworks to evaluate trade promotion effectiveness, measure spending efficiency, and maximize return on investment (ROI).
Accrual & Close Governance: Evaluate and assess outstanding trade expense commitments to inform trade accruals during the periodic close process ensuring compliance with internal governance.
Overhead & A&CP Partnership: Provide financial governance over commercial overhead structures and partner with marketing teams to manage Advertising & Consumer Promotion (A&CP) budgets and drive actionable insights
Integrated Business Planning & S&OP+ Integration
S&OP+ Demand Management Review (DMR): Serve as the core finance representative for Step 2 of the S&OP+ cycle (Demand Management Review). Synthesize operating plans and market assumptions to align sales forecasts with corporate financial commitments.
Strategic Business Planning: Conduct market research, financial modeling, and scenario analysis to assist in the development and execution of the annual and multi-year Business Plans.
Innovation Evaluation: Provide financial assessments, business case modeling, and post-launch performance analysis for local innovation pipelines to ensure margin-accretive growth.
Financial Analysis, Reporting & Performance Tracking
Forecast & Trend Analysis: Provide timely and accurate financial forecasts, month-end variance analyses, and commentary regarding prevailing business trends and market drivers.
Performance Indicators: Define, calculate, and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs), financial benchmarks, and performance scorecards to hold the commercial business accountable.
Executive & Ad Hoc Reporting: Prepare executive-ready reports, business reviews, and ad hoc financial analyses to support key decisions by the leadership team.
Collaboration & Team Leadership
Cross-Functional Partnership: Build trusted relationships across Sales, Marketing, Category Management, and Demand teams, providing both constructive challenge and financial leadership.
Global FP&A Liaison: Collaborate with Regional and Global FP&A teams to integrate local performance reporting into global rhythms and standardize financial frameworks.
Staff Guidance: Provide coaching, training, and professional guidance to junior finance staff or cross-functional team members to elevate financial acumen across the organization.
Requirements
Education & Credentials Required: Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business, Economics, or a related analytical field.
Preferred: MBA, CPA, CA, or equivalent professional credentials.
Experience Professional Experience: 6+ years of progressive finance experience, with a heavy emphasis on commercial finance, sales finance, trade management, or financial planning.
Industry Context: Experience within a Fast-Moving Consumer Goods (FMCG), Consumer Packaged Goods (CPG), or Food & Beverage environment is highly preferred.

Industry Competitive Benefits:  Medical, dental, vision and employee assistance programs to meet your individual or family needs.
Continuing Education:  In house & online learning & development, as well as an education assistance program.
Quality:  a dedication to uphold the highest standards of authenticity, nutritional integrity, and food safety, to earn the trust of Pet Lovers everywhere.
Other Perks:  Free bag of premium pet food each month.

Mars Wrigley is looking to hire a Facilities Technician at our climate-controlled Topeka, KS location!
The Facilities Technician is responsible for the operation and reliability of all plant systems including high pressure boilers, chillers, cooling towers, air compressors, HVAC systems, Wastewater Treatment (WWT), Ammonia, and facility power supply equipment and processes. The Facilities Technician must possess multi-craft skills (Mechanical and Electrical) and be able to troubleshoot and make repairs to a wide variety of equipment in a safe and efficient manner. This role requires knowledge, competency, professionalism, and safety consciousness to optimize equipment efficiency and longevity while assuring product quality. The Facilities Technician must be able to function with little or no supervision.
This position is responsible for local, state, and federal environmental compliance through internal and external audits and networking with regulators, insurers, and other industry representatives. The Utilities Technician assures adherence to ISO and Mars Wrigley Confectionery Conservation standards. Requirements also include the areas of reliable routine service, timely backlog management and prompt emergency response. The Facilities Technician provides technical knowledge for diagnosing, troubleshooting, repairing and debugging complex utilities issues, computer systems, and/or software. They perform emergency repairs on utilities equipment in a quick, efficient, and safe manner, continuously makes decisions in order of prioritizing tasks to sustain plant operations and production.
Key Responsibilities:
Provide & maintains Steam, Compressed Air, Plant Environmental Conditioning, Fire Protection, Weather protection, and Wastewater Treatment, crucial to plant operation.
Demonstrated expertise in advanced troubleshooting and resolution of system-wide or area-wide, chronic problems in processes and products.
Ensures that the jobs listed in the Daily Shift Checks manual are performed efficiently and in a timely manner. This consists of but is not limited to: Shift checks and logging of equipment operation, chemical testing of boiler and loop systems, assuring safe and efficient operation as well as maintenance of the Boilers and their sub equipment, Chillers and sub equipment, Air compressors and sub equipment, Environmental Air Handler units and sub equipment as well as assist at the WWT if needed.
Ensure adherence to the various operating permits and required inspections mandated by Federal, State, and Local authorities. These include Air, Wastewater, Pressure Vessels, Refrigeration, Storm water and Spill Prevention Control and Countermeasure Plan, by actively following ISO 9000/14001 Standards.
Ensure optimum efficiency of all plant utilities, and wastewater equipment, through preventive/predictive methods. Optimizes preventive maintenance procedures and performs these tasks on assigned area/ systems. Focuses on completion of system generated PM’s and assigned Work Orders. Initiate new PM’s or modify existing PM’s to ensure system optimization.
Maintain an “inspection-ready” site with respect to operational and environmental compliance.

Works on complex problems.

Trains other team members. Represents utilities in cross-functional meetings to provide experience from a technical point of view.
Willing to participate in the selection process of new technicians, when applicable.
Must be able to efficiently meet all the requirements of a facilities technician.

Standing on a concrete floor.
Wearing proper personal protective equipment (hair net, bump cap, ear plugs, safety shoes, and uniform).
Bending, stooping, twist, turn, standing for extended time periods, reaching, climbing stairs, and lifting up to 50 lbs.

1+ years of maintenance experience
Standing on a concrete floor.

Bending, stooping, twist, turn, standing for extended time periods, reaching, climbing stairs, and lifting up to 50 lbs.

Working for extended periods under elevated levels of ambient noise, heat, and light due to necessary equipment and ventilation systems.

As a Mechanical Designer – Cryomechanical Systems You will own products from cradle to grave, working hands on to oversee initial builds, incorporating customer feedback to make improvements and driving continuous improvements to equipment as the state-of-the-art advances. You help shape requirements, create complete three-dimensional (3D) models from scratch, produce two-dimensional (2D) drawings, document Bill of Materials (BOM), create standard operating procedures (SOPs) and work hands on in installations to guide products through their entire lifecycle.
At Microsoft, our mission—to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more—guides how we partner with customers to deliver trusted, impactful solutions. Own end-to-end three-dimensional (3D) computer-aided design (CAD) for cryogenic subassemblies and top-level mechanical integrations, including cold fingers, millikelvin (mK) and 4 kelvin (4 K) stages, radiation shields, vacuum interfaces, and cable or harness routing fixtures; create fully detailed two-dimensional (2D) drawings with geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T) and tolerance stackups.
Build and steward the top assembly and bill of materials (BOM) by managing part numbering, configurations, engineering change order (ECO) and engineering change request (ECR) workflows, and product data management/product lifecycle management (PDM/PLM) toolchains such as SolidWorks, Windchill, and OnePDM.

description:
Overview
The Online Forensics team sits within the Microsoft AI Experiences organization, where we protect the monetization network that funds the products people use every day. Because attackers adapt quickly, effective defense requires discovering how systems can be abused, not just investigating known incidents. We combine hands-on adversarial research, controlled experimentation, and large-scale data analysis to establish authoritative ground truth and expose weaknesses before they are exploited at scale.
As a Principal Applied Scientist, you will discover how web-based monetization systems can be manipulated and build the experimental and investigation systems needed to study that abuse at scale. Your research will cover both exploitable weaknesses and abuse of intended functionality, including automation, identity and attribution manipulation, and multi-step economic exploitation. You will personally write code, construct safe adversarial experiments, and combine experimental evidence with large-scale telemetry to establish mechanism, prevalence, and impact.
The scientific challenge is to distinguish adversarial manipulation from legitimate behavior under incomplete and potentially manipulated telemetry. You will develop methods to test competing explanations, determine whether experimental findings generalize to real-world traffic, and evaluate candidate signals without unacceptable false positives. You will turn validated approaches into reliable, reusable systems and evaluation methods that partner defense teams can adopt.
You will own a focused portfolio of high-impact research problems, from hypothesis through implementation, validation, and adoption. At the principal level, you will set scientific and technical direction while remaining directly involved in coding, experimentation, debugging, and delivery. You will own the research capabilities you build; partner defense teams own production enforcement and remediation.

Personally implement adversarial experiments. Build automated clients, instrumented browser workflows, simulations, and replay harnesses under safe, authorized conditions with clear scope and safeguards. Use appropriate controls and competing hypotheses to distinguish demonstrated mechanisms from unvalidated assumptions.
Develop rigorous evaluation methods. Assess whether experiments represent real-world conditions, establish the provenance and quality of labels, and measure generalization, coverage, false-positive risk, and robustness to adaptation.
Build durable research and investigation systems. Design, implement, test, deploy, and maintain the services, instrumentation, telemetry pipelines, and reusable libraries needed for the research portfolio. Turn successful approaches into reliable capabilities that other researchers and partner teams can use independently.
Connect experiments to real-world evidence. Apply behavioral, graph-based, temporal, and cross-surface analysis to large-scale telemetry. Identify adversary infrastructure and evasion patterns, determine prevalence, and quantify economic exposure while stating uncertainty and limitations.
Establish authoritative ground truth. Correlate evidence across accounts, traffic, transactions, providers, devices, and infrastructure. Reconstruct attack chains and produce reproducible datasets and technical assessments that clearly state mechanism, provenance, confidence, scale, and impact.
Translate findings into stronger defenses. Produce candidate signals, labeled evaluation datasets, monitored indicators, and reproducible regression scenarios. Partner with teams that own production defenses to evaluate improvements and verify that corrective actions address the demonstrated abuse.
Lead scientific and technical work. As a Senior Mechanical Designer – Cryomechanical Systems You will own products from cradle to grave, working hands on to oversee initial builds, incorporating customer feedback to make improvements and driving continuous improvements to equipment as the state-of-the-art advances. You help shape requirements, create complete three-dimensional (3D) models from scratch, produce two-dimensional (2D) drawings, document Bill of Materials (BOM), create standard operating procedures (SOPs) and work hands on in installations to guide products through their entire lifecycle.
Microsoft’s culture is grounded in a growth mindset, customer obsession, diversity and inclusion, one Microsoft collaboration, and making a difference through technology. Own end-to-end three-dimensional (3D) computer-aided design (CAD) for cryogenic subassemblies and top-level mechanical integrations, including cold fingers, millikelvin (mK) and 4 kelvin (4 K) stages, radiation shields, vacuum interfaces, and cable or harness routing fixtures; create fully detailed two-dimensional (2D) drawings with geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T) and tolerance stackups.

Create SOPs by making detailed work instructions for installing parts, recording key data during installation and making sure that engineering intent is effectively communicated to engineers and technicians in the field.
Drive design for manufacturing/design for excellence (DFM/DFX) with suppliers by generating clear build packages, supporting fabrication through first-article approval, dispositioning nonconformances with data-driven tolerance and fit assessments, and capturing as-built changes in drawings and bills of materials (BOMs).

title: Senior Software Engineer
description:
Overview
The Agent 365 Foundation team builds and operates the platform layer that keeps agent workloads reliable, secure, and fast at Microsoft scale. Our charter within this group is traffic ingress: every request that reaches our clusters passes through the gateway and edge systems we own. We are the front door, which means we are also the first line of defense and the first place a problem shows up.
A significant part of our current focus is ingress for Dynamics 365 and Power Platform traffic. That work spans routing and gateway policy, connection and protocol handling, tenant isolation, throttling and abuse mitigation, failover behavior across regions, and the observability needed to reason about all of it while it is happening. The scale is large, the traffic patterns are diverse, and the correctness bar is high.
About the Role
We are hiring a Senior Software Engineer to design, build, and operate the gateway and ingress path end to end. This is a hands-on engineering role. You will spend your time in code, in design reviews, and in production — writing services in C# and Go, tuning TLS and HTTP/2 behavior, shaping how gRPC traffic flows through the stack, working with Azure Front Door and our own edge components, and hardening the system against volumetric and application-layer attacks.
You will own outcomes rather than tickets. That means choosing where resiliency belongs in the request path, deciding what a safe failure mode looks like for a given class of traffic, and defending those decisions with data. You will also be part of the on-call rotation for the systems you build, because the fastest way to build a resilient front door is to feel it when it bends.
Who Thrives in This Role
The engineer who does well here is genuinely hands-on. You are comfortable being the person who reads the proxy source, reproduces the failure locally, and lands the fix — seniority here means more time close to the system, not less. You think critically about problems before reaching for a solution, ask what the data actually shows, and are willing to challenge a design, including your own, when the evidence points elsewhere.
You also do not shy away from hard problems. Ambiguous incidents, legacy traffic paths, unfamiliar protocol behavior, and difficult cross-team conversations are part of the work, and you move toward them rather than around them. You are direct, collaborative, and comfortable operating with a high degree of ownership.
Why This Role Matters
Ingress is where reliability and security are decided for everything behind it. The work you do here is visible in the availability numbers of some of Microsoft's largest business platforms, and it is felt immediately by the customers who depend on them. If you want a role where deep networking expertise, sound judgment, and engineering craft compound into real impact, this is it.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
Responsibilities
Design, implement, and operate L4 and L7 ingress components — gateways, proxies, load balancing and routing policy — that carry Dynamics 365 and Power Platform traffic into our clusters.
Own the protocol layer: TLS termination and certificate lifecycle, HTTP/2 connection management, gRPC routing and streaming behavior, and the performance characteristics of each.
Build resiliency into the request path through health-based routing, retries and hedging, circuit breaking, load shedding, rate limiting, and regional failover, and prove the behavior through fault injection and load testing.
Strengthen the security posture of the edge, including DDoS detection and mitigation, WAF and abuse-mitigation policy, tenant isolation, and defense against application-layer attack patterns.
Integrate and tune Azure Front Door and related edge services alongside our first-party gateway components, and make deliberate decisions about which layer solves which problem.
Instrument the ingress path so that latency, error, and saturation questions can be answered in minutes, and drive incident response, root-cause analysis, and the follow-through that keeps the same failure from repeating.
Partner with service teams across Dynamics 365, Power Platform, and Agent 365 on onboarding, capacity, and traffic-shaping decisions, and raise the engineering bar through design and code review.
Qualifications
Required Qualifications:

At Microsoft Quantum, we aim to empower science and scientists to solve the world’s biggest problems by realizing advanced computing platforms at the intersection of high-performance computing, artificial intelligence, and quantum information technology. The Cryomechanical team enables Microsoft Quantum’s hardware roadmap by designing, integrating, and sustaining cryogenic mechanical systems, packaging solutions, and laboratory infrastructure that support reliable experimentation, scalable system integration, and disciplined transition from research concepts to producible hardware.
As a Simulation Engineer – Mechanical & Thermal Systems , you will lead mechanical, structural, thermal, and coupled multiphysics analysis for cryogenic hardware and laboratory systems using COMSOL Multiphysics and ANSYS. You will translate system requirements and design concepts into verified computational models, quantify margins and sensitivities, correlate predictions with test data, and deliver clear engineering recommendations that guide architecture, detailed design, manufacturing, integration, and root-cause investigations throughout the product lifecycle.
Microsoft’s culture is grounded in a growth mindset, customer obsession, diversity and inclusion, one Microsoft collaboration, and making a difference through technology. In this role, you will be expected to model these values by learning continuously, partnering across disciplines, communicating clearly, and creating an inclusive environment where rigorous engineering and shared accountability help the team deliver meaningful impact.
Responsibilities
Own end-to-end mechanical and thermal analysis for cryogenic subassemblies and top-level integrations, including millikelvin (mK), 4 kelvin (4 K), and ambient-temperature structures, radiation shields, vacuum interfaces, thermal straps, supports, and cable or harness routing hardware.
Develop and maintain high-fidelity finite element and multiphysics models in COMSOL Multiphysics and ANSYS Mechanical, including defensible geometry idealization, material models, contacts, interfaces, meshing strategies, loads, boundary conditions, solver controls, and post-processing methods.

Verify, validate, and correlate simulation results through mesh-convergence studies, sensitivity and uncertainty analyses, hand calculations, analytical benchmarks, and comparison with instrumentation, prototype, and system-level test data.
Drive design decisions through clear technical communication by presenting assumptions, methods, limitations, margins, risks, and recommendations at design reviews; partner with mechanical designers, thermal engineers, physicists, electrical engineers, manufacturing teams, and suppliers to close issues and improve designs.

title: Business Development Lead, Life Sciences
description:
About the Team

OpenAI’s Partnerships team develops external relationships that advance our research and products and expand how organizations can benefit from AI. Within life sciences, we work across pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies, AI-native discovery platforms, research institutions, and experimental labs. We partner closely with Research, Product, Engineering, Safety, GTM, Legal, and Finance to turn complex scientific, technical, and commercial opportunities into durable partnerships.

About the Role

We are hiring a Life Sciences Partnerships Lead to shape and execute OpenAI’s global life sciences partnership strategy. You will lead high-impact research, product, and platform partnerships across the life sciences ecosystem.

You will help determine where OpenAI should invest deeply with strategic partners, where we should enable a broader ecosystem, and how research, product, safety, and commercial considerations should shape our decisions. You will bring the voice of life sciences partners into OpenAI while helping internal teams turn ambiguous opportunities into clear decisions and executable plans.

This role requires scientific and commercial fluency, strong judgment, and the ability to move complex partnerships from strategy through execution and measurable impact.

In this role, you will:

 - Lead full-lifecycle strategic partnerships, from partner strategy and executive alignment through scoping, commercial negotiation, execution, and ongoing operating reviews.

 - Identify and prioritize opportunities across pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies, AI-native discovery platforms, research institutions, and experimental labs.

 - Work closely with Research, Product, and Engineering to translate partner needs, scientific workflows, technical constraints, and market dynamics into product and program recommendations.

 - Partner with Legal, Finance, Safety, Research, and other cross-functional teams to structure partnerships with the appropriate data, deployment, governance, and commercial models.

 - Coordinate with Health, GTM, GSI/MSSP enablement, and cloud service provider partnership teams to turn strategic relationships into broader ecosystem adoption and measurable impact.

 - Build trusted relationships with senior executives, scientific leaders, and technical counterparts across the life sciences ecosystem.

 - Bring structure to ambiguous opportunities, clear blockers across internal and external teams, and communicate decisions and tradeoffs clearly to senior leaders.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Have 12+ years of experience in strategic partnerships, product partnerships, business development, or general management across the life sciences and technology industries.

 - Bring a deep understanding of the life sciences ecosystem, including its scientific workflows, business models, incentives, and key industry dynamics.

 - Have led complex strategic partnerships spanning research or scientific collaboration, technical execution, commercial terms, go-to-market strategy, and long-term platform alignment.

title: Product Data Scientist - Youth, Families and Learning
description:
About the role

We’re looking for a product data scientist to help OpenAI create more value and drive sustainable growth for young people, families, and learners. You’ll drive product data science across under-18 audiences, emerging opportunities for children under 13, family experiences, and learning and education more broadly.

You’ll help decide where we should invest, what we should build, and how we’ll know it is working. This means understanding distinct audience needs, identifying promising use cases, and turning evidence into a clear product strategy. Your work will connect discovery and early product development with adoption, retention, and sustained user value.

You’ll partner across Chat Product, Growth, Foundations, SafeSys, and other teams, working closely with product managers, engineers, designers, and researchers. The role focuses and owns product value and growth while dedicated teams own policy and safety.

In this role, you will:

 - Shape strategy and prioritize opportunities. Size unmet needs and growth opportunities across audiences, use cases, and product experiences. Help teams choose where to invest and sequence work based on expected user value, reach, evidence, and effort.

 - Define what value and success mean. Develop an audience-specific measurement framework spanning activation, task success, learning progress, satisfaction, and durable retention. Connect these measures to product goals and assess whether repeat use reflects meaningful benefit.

 - Understand users and growth drivers. Analyze journeys, funnels, and cohorts to uncover where people find value, where they struggle, and what helps them return. Combine behavioral data with surveys and user research to explain differences across ages, family roles, and learning contexts.

 - Measure what changes actually cause. Design experiments and holdouts to evaluate product and model changes. Apply causal methods when randomization is impractical, make assumptions explicit, and account for seasonality, audience composition, and effects that differ across segments.

 - Turn findings into product decisions. Work with partners from initial hypotheses through launch and iteration. Recommend what to build, change, expand, or stop, explaining expected impact, uncertainty, and tradeoffs. Follow through to determine whether decisions delivered the intended results.

 - Build reliable measurement. Partner with engineering on instrumentation, dataset quality, and consistent audience definitions. Create reusable analyses and dashboards that make progress visible and let teams answer recurring questions independently.

 - Create alignment across teams. Bring a coherent view of audience value to work spanning multiple roadmaps. Help partners agree on priorities, success criteria, and the next questions to resolve, even when ownership is distributed and evidence is incomplete.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

 - A record of influencing product strategy and improving user outcomes through hands-on data science, including work from an ambiguous question to a decision and measurable impact.

 - Strong SQL and Python skills, sound statistical judgment, and practical experience with experiments, causal inference, cohort analysis, and measurement design.

 - The ability to develop useful definitions of product value, validate imperfect proxies, and distinguish short-term metric movement from lasting improvement.

 - Clear communication and strong product judgment. You can make a recommendation, explain its limits, and influence collaborators across functions without relying on formal authority.

 - Comfort setting priorities independently across a broad scope, staying close to users, and moving between strategic questions and detailed analytical work.

Helpful experience

Experience with consumer product growth, youth or family products, learning and education, or generative AI would be valuable. We also welcome experience measuring learning outcomes, combining quantitative and qualitative research, or evaluating products whose value emerges over time.

description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

Our Inference team brings OpenAI’s most capable research and technology to the world through our products. We empower consumers, enterprises and developers alike to use and access our state-of-the-art AI models, allowing them to do things that they’ve never been able to before. We focus on performant and efficient model inference, as well as accelerating research progression via model inference.

We’re looking for an engineer to lead the optimization of OpenAI’s state-of-the-art frontier models on TPUs. You will own performance across the full forward pass, from model code through kernels to execution on the hardware.

You’ll have broad technical ownership: identifying performance bottlenecks, choosing the most impactful improvements, and carrying them through implementation and validation. We welcome experience gained through either training or inference, with a strong foundation in optimizing real workloads on TPUs.

 - Optimize model execution on TPUs, improving performance across the complete forward pass and the interactions between model code, kernels, and hardware.

 - Profile workloads, identify bottlenecks, and implement improvements to latency, throughput, and hardware utilization.

 - Develop and optimize kernels, using an understanding of the surrounding model to guide implementation choices.

 - Explore techniques such as quantization to improve inference efficiency while preserving model quality.

 - Build benchmarks and tools to measure performance, validate correctness, and guide optimization work.

 - Partner with researchers and engineers to support new model architectures and bring performance improvements into production.

 - Have practical experience optimizing machine learning workloads on TPUs, through training, inference, or both.

 - Understand modern model architectures and how their computation maps onto accelerator hardware.

 - Can connect detailed kernel behavior to the performance of a complete model and work across these layers of the stack.

 - Bring strong software engineering skills and a systematic approach to profiling, debugging, and validating performance improvements.

 - Take ownership of open-ended technical problems and can identify priorities, make design decisions, and deliver working solutions.

location: Carneys Point, New Jersey, United States
description:
ABOUT QUINCE
Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world’s finest products. From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes  and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast.
What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver.
OUR CULTURE
Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. We question conventional thinking, use technology and data to uncover new opportunities, and move quickly to turn ideas into reality. We aren’t interested in replicating how others do retail. We’re building a better way – at a speed and scale unlike anything that’s been done before.
We dream big and chase the hard problems others shy away from. Rejecting long-held assumptions is part of our company's DNA.  Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place.
Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths.
Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory.
If you’re someone who likes to imagine new possibilities and build better systems rather than plug-in to outdated ones, Quince is the place for you.
THE ROLE
Warehouse Associate – Day Shift
Location: 24 N Game Creek Road, Carney’s Point, NJ 08069 | Full Time | $20.50/hr days ($22.50/hr nights) | Shift: Front half days & back half days
Why You’ll Want This Job
Great pay that grows. Start at $20.50/hr on days, with raises up to $23/hr. No guesswork—you’ll know exactly when and how your pay increases.
Hours you can count on. Guaranteed minimum hours and a consistent schedule, so you can plan your life. Want more? Overtime is available.
Paid training from day one. No warehouse experience? No problem. We’ll teach you everything you need to succeed.
Room to move up. We’re growing fast, and we promote from within.
A team that has your back. You’ll work alongside people who help each other out—not just clock in and out.
What You’ll Do
Every day is a little different, and we’ll train you on all of it:
Receive, unpack, and inspect merchandise using easy-to-learn computer systems
Pick, pack, and ship customer orders
Process returns and keep inventory accurate
Team up with fellow associates and flag issues to your manager
Jump into different assignments as needed—variety keeps the shift moving
What We’re Looking For
Reliable and detail-oriented
Comfortable working both independently and with a team
Open to overtime when it’s available
Able to stand and walk for a full shift; push, pull, bend, and reach throughout the day; lift up to 49 lbs. and push carts up to 60 lbs. (with or without accommodations)

Joining Quince means being part of a mission-driven team reshaping retail. You will work alongside talented colleagues, tackle meaningful challenges, and contribute to building a more sustainable, accessible future for customers and partners alike.

title: AI Data Operation Lead,  Autonomy
description: About Rivian Rivian is on a mission to keep the world adventurous forever. This goes for the emissions-free Electric Adventure Vehicles we build, and the curious, courageous souls we seek to attract. As a company, we constantly challenge what’s possible, never simply accepting what has always been done. We reframe old problems, seek new solutions and operate comfortably in areas that are unknown. Our backgrounds are diverse, but our team shares a love of the outdoors and a desire to protect it for future generations. Role Summary Rivian Autonomy is seeking an AI Data Operation Lead to lead the people and processes that turn vehicle data into reliable training and evaluation datasets. Within the AI Platform organization, you will bring together labeling delivery, data quality, curation, and human review to support the development of our autonomous driving models. You will lead internal teams and external partners, with accountability for delivery, quality, and cost. This includes making sure the data we send for annotation is usable, that accepted labels meet the model teams' requirements, and that reviewers can turn difficult driving events into actionable feedback for engineering. You will work closely with Perception, Planning, Data Infrastructure, Eval Infrastructure, and Product to translate model-development priorities into operational plans and provide evidence for release decisions. We are looking for a leader who can develop managers and specialists, make clear tradeoffs when demand exceeds capacity, and build an operation that improves as our models, tools, and vehicle fleet evolve. Responsibilities Lead the organization. Set the operating plan for AI data operations, develop team leaders, and define responsibilities across employees, contractors, and vendors. Build capacity plans that account for annotation, quality review, and rework across concurrent programs. Deliver data that model teams can use. Translate training and evaluation needs into labeling specifications, reviewer guidance, delivery milestones, and acceptance criteria. Work with model teams on taxonomy changes and keep delivery aligned with their development cycles. Improve data quality and yield. Own the operational checks that determine whether collected vehicle data is ready for curation and labeling. Partner with collection and engineering teams to resolve sensor, calibration, and data-quality issues before they consume downstream annotation capacity. Own vendor performance and spend. Set service levels and quality expectations, evaluate suppliers, and manage capacity, pricing, and budgets with Finance and Procurement. Reconcile accepted work with invoices and address delivery or quality shortfalls through clear corrective actions. Develop human evaluation and triage operations. Build review workflows with autonomy and systems engineers to investigate driving events, classify recurring failures, and assemble the evidence needed for root-cause analysis. Feed those findings into scenario selection, evaluation datasets, and targeted data requests. Run the operation with consistent metrics. Establish a shared view of accepted-data volume, quality, turnaround time, backlog, rework, collection yield, and cost. Use these measures to identify constraints, allocate review capacity, and make delivery commitments teams can plan around. Improve tools and automation. Partner with Data Infrastructure, Eval Infrastructure, and Applied General AI on labeling tools, prelabels, automated quality checks, and assisted triage. Define operational requirements and validate improvements against measured quality and reviewer effort before scaling them. Qualifications 10+ years leading operations, including at least 5 years supporting autonomous vehicles, robotics, or complex machine-learning programs, with responsibility for budgets or a P&L. Experience managing annotation partners across domestic and international locations, including commercial negotiations, staffing plans, and service delivery. Enough technical depth in AI development to discuss data requirements and failure analysis with engineers and turn those discussions into clear work for operations teams. A record of developing managers and specialists, establishing ownership, and adapting team structures as priorities change. Strong analytical judgment: you can separate a quality problem from a capacity or tooling problem, test the cause, and follow through on the fix. Clear communication across engineering, product, finance, and operations, with the ability to make prioritization decisions and explain their impact on delivery. Bonus Points Direct experience supporting autonomous driving or other physical AI systems through data production and evaluation. Experience applying large language models, multimodal models, or generative AI to annotation and human-review workflows. description:
Who we are
Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.
About the role:
R&D Enablement helps our Product, Engineering, and Design teams build the capabilities, access the knowledge, and develop the ways of working required to deliver for our customers. We are looking for a Principal, R&D Learning Products & Enablement to define the future of this function: understand how R&D teams work, identify the highest-value capability and performance needs, and translate emerging technologies and business priorities into scalable learning products and enablement solutions.
This is a senior, hands-on individual contributor role for someone who can move between strategy, technical product understanding, learning-product design, and end-to-end program delivery. You will build and prioritize the R&D Enablement roadmap; create tools, automations, knowledge solutions, and learning experiences; and work directly with R&D leaders, engineers, technology vendors, Global Learning & Development, People, and Business Technology partners to bring the right solutions to life.
This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the United States.
You should apply if:
You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact – helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, reduce emissions, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won’t be your last at Samsara. We set up our employees for success and have built a culture that encourages rapid career development, countless opportunities to experiment and master your craft in a hyper growth environment.
You’re energized by our opportunity: The vision we have to digitize large sectors of the global economy requires your full focus and best efforts to bring forth creative, ambitious ideas for our customers.
You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. You will be surrounded by a high-calibre team that will encourage you to do your best.
In this role, you will:
Define the R&D learning-products and enablement strategy, roadmap, service model, and measures of success by developing a representative understanding of the needs of R&D employees and leaders at all levels.
Build trusted relationships across R&D and conduct discovery to identify the most important capability, knowledge, adoption, and performance needs.
Diagnose whether the appropriate solution is a learning experience, structured knowledge, workflow change, automation, self-service tool, community, manager resource, or another intervention.
Stay current on emerging technologies, AI models, developer tools, and changes in how technical teams work; translate those developments into practical recommendations for how R&D employees can use AI and agents, validate their outputs, and determine where automation is appropriate versus where human judgment, expertise, or coordination remains essential.
Build alongside R&D employees, technical leaders, Business Technology, Security, enterprise AI teams, and external technology providers to move high-value ideas from concept to practical tools, workflows, prototypes, and scalable adoption.
Translate complex technical concepts into scalable learning products, developer-onboarding experiences, knowledge resources, playbooks, tools, automations, and communities that help R&D employees learn and self-serve.
Create and test functional prototypes, tools, and workflow automations using AI-assisted development environments, APIs, low-code platforms, and other appropriate technologies.
Develop clear product and program requirements, user stories, workflows, success criteria, and implementation plans for solutions requiring support from Engineering or Business Technology.
Lead complex programs from discovery through launch and adoption, establishing clear ownership, milestones, dependencies, risks, communications, feedback loops, and decision points across interdependent teams.
Make informed recommendations about what to build, configure, buy, integrate, transfer, scale, or stop.
Own and continuously improve R&D and developer onboarding, ensuring employees can efficiently access the systems, knowledge, resources, and communities required to become productive.
Define outcome measures that go beyond attendance and satisfaction, using adoption, behavior, capability, time-to-proficiency, self-service, efficiency, quality, and business evidence to determine whether solutions should continue, change, scale, transfer, or stop.

title: Welding Sales Manager
description:
About Standard Bots

Standard Bots is America's largest manufacturer of AI-native industrial robots. Full-stack robots—hardware, software, and AI—all designed and assembled in Glen Cove, New York. The company makes AI-native robots anyone can buy and deploy, with customers ranging from family-owned machine shops to the Fortune 500. Customers include Sunoco, Lockheed Martin, NASA, and the U.S. Army, along with hundreds of manufacturers nationwide. Standard Bots raised a $200 million Series C at a $1 billion valuation from RoboStrategy, General Catalyst, Amazon Industrial Innovation Fund, and Samsung Next.


About the role

Fabricators across the country can't hire enough welders, and you know it better than most, because you've run a torch yourself. As our Welding Sales Manager, you'll show shops what cobot welding does for their throughput, quality, and people, and you'll own the national welding number. Welding is one of our fastest-growing applications, and you'll be the person who helps it grow even faster.


📍 Location

This role is remote within the United States, and we prefer candidates in NYC metro, North Carolina, California, Illinois or Texas. Expect to travel frequently to customer sites, regional teams, trade shows, and partners (~50% domestic travel).


What you'll do

- Own the welding number. You carry the national quota for welding systems and revenue across direct and partner sales. You build and manage the welding pipeline and forecast with each region, and you measure success by installed, producing systems, not just bookings.

- Partner with Regional Sales Managers. You co-sell welding opportunities with RSMs in every territory, from discovery through close. That means welding-specific discovery, part and joint reviews, and ROI conversations with fabricators. You'll join customer site visits, demos, and weld trials alongside our Welding Applications Engineers, and you'll raise the welding knowledge of the broader sales team through training, deal reviews, and ride-alongs.

- Sell direct MIG welding systems. You help shops evaluate cobot MIG welding against their part mix, volumes, and labor constraints, and you lead the proposals, pricing, and negotiation on welding deals.

- Build the partner channel. You recruit and manage gas and welding distributors as a lead source for Standard Bots welding. You also support partner-built solutions, such as laser welding cells, from the first conversation to repeatable sales.

- Be the voice of the welding customer. You bring field feedback on ease of use, features, and competitive gaps to the welding product team, and you represent Standard Bots at welding and fabrication trade shows and industry events.


What you'll bring

- Hands-on welding experience. You've laid beads and you know what a good weld looks like. MIG is required; TIG or laser is a plus.

- 5+ years in welding sales or welding applications, ideally robotic or automated welding.

- A track record of closing capital equipment deals with manufacturers and fabricators.

- Comfort working as an individual contributor who leads through influence across regional sales teams.

- Willingness to travel frequently to customer sites, trade shows, and partner meetings.


Nice to have

- Experience with a welding OEM, welding distributor, or robotic welding integrator.

- Existing relationships with gas and welding distributors.

- AWS certification (CW, CWI, or similar).

- Experience building or managing a channel partner program.


Compensation and Benefits

The on target earnings (OTE) range for this role is $190,000 - $225,000, depending on experience. We are open to a variety of seniority levels for this role and will build compensation packages that are commensurate with seniority and skill level. Base salary is just one part of the overall compensation at Standard Bots. All Full-Time Employees are eligible for Employee Stock Options. We also offer a package of benefits including paid time off, medical/dental/vision insurance, life insurance, disability insurance, and 401(k) to regular full-time employees.

valuate manufacturability, backward compatibility, service installation, spare-parts strategy, inventory disposition, and implementation risk.
